_about: Discovery partitions (devops/discovery_plan.py). One lane per job site, never mixed. partitions: how many independent machines read that site's boards; max_partitions: the most it may ever be split into; budget: the most boards of that site read at the same moment across ALL its partitions (one_host sites: machines asking the one host at once, each keeping the 1.5 s gap). lane "mac": the site is read on the Mac, outside the cloud fetch (its boards are still counted in the coverage, as planned on the Mac). probe_quota: when the site's last cloud run was refused for at least probe_when_refused of its boards (HTTP 429 through every retry), only this many of its boards are asked, the least recently read first, until it answers again. quota: the most of the site's boards one cloud run asks, the least recently read first, so every board takes its turn; the rest are deferred by quota, never called failed. A site not listed gets one partition. queue_minutes: the site's last measured minutes per partition (26 Nov 2026 run 45903934655; Lever, Ashby and Jobvite: expected at their new splits) -- the order the matrix is started in, longest first, since only 19 partitions run at once. readers_per_runner: logical partitions run side by side on one GitHub runner (devops/discovery_plan.py bundles), never two of one site, each its own process and client. max_rps: the site's total request-rate cap across all its readers and runners (each reader keeps partitions / max_rps seconds between any two requests), so adding machines never raises it. in_run_retry false: a refused board is not waited for and asked again in the same run; a later run reads it first.
_history: Nov 2026, owner-approved: Greenhouse 3, Lever 2, Ashby 2 machines, one board at a time each (about 1.6, 1.1 and 1.1 requests a second to each host in all, watched for 429s, each machine backing off on its own); Workable and Jobvite on a quota (Workable refused nearly every request). 25 Nov 2026 (cloud-only discovery, owner's scope): Workday back in the cloud -- every site is read by the cloud, never by the Mac. Its boards were read from GitHub without refusal until mid-November, then refused nearly every time; while it refuses, a probe of its least recently read boards is asked each run. Time budget 90 minutes: the run starts at 1:00 or 11:00 Central and must be published within two hours. 26 Nov 2026 (Development Mode, owner-approved): Greenhouse 6 machines made the baseline after the measured run (22.4 min, no 429s, same coverage). Experiments, each kept only if measured better: Lever 4 and Ashby 4 machines (one board at a time each, about 2x their earlier request rates), Jobvite every board on 3 machines instead of 150 a run on one (it refused nothing). 26 Nov 2026 run 45909763192: Lever 4 (11.8-12.0 min, 0 refusals) and Ashby 4 (12.0-12.2 min, 0 refusals) kept, coverage unchanged; Jobvite on 3 kept for coverage (480 of 536 read, from 150; 7 refused requests); GitHub gave only 10 runners at first, so partitions are now grouped, up to 3 a runner, never two of one site. Experiment: Recruitee on 2 machines (3 workers each, budget unchanged) -- it was refused 357-385 times a run from one machine. 26 Nov 2026 run 45914877636 (runners grouped): 25.8 min, 85.8% read; Recruitee on 2 machines 2.9 min (from 20.3; 58-59 refusals each, from 357-385 on one) kept. Experiment: Greenhouse 9 machines (about 4.7 requests a second to its host, 0 refusals at 6) and BambooHR 4 machines with 3 workers each (budget 12: each machine as before, twice the machines). 26 Nov 2026 run 45918003480: Greenhouse 9 (14.8-15.0 min, 0 refusals, every board) and BambooHR 4 (11.9 min, 0 refusals) kept; 21.2 min to publish. Site-wide caps set at or just under the measured refusal-free rates (Greenhouse 5, Lever and Ashby 2.5 requests a second, unchanged in practice); Recruitee capped at 2 a second and Jobvite at 1.3, below the rates at which they refused; Workday's refused probe boards are no longer waited for in the run (0 of 40 recovered in every measured run).
